game.name: Sundered®: Eldritch Edition
game.short_description: Sundered is a chaotic hand­-drawn metroidvania where you resist or embrace ancient eldritch powers, a challenging and unique take on a classic genre from the creators of Jotun, now with local co-op!

other_scores.source: Steam user reviews (Very Positive, about 82% of roughly 5,200)

placements.verbal_evidence: it's going to be a low B tier

commentary.label: Tier list Part 1 (2023)
commentary.summary: Sundered is a Metroidvania with roguelike elements bolted on. He thinks the visuals, world and story make a great Metroidvania, but the roguelike layer feels like a last-second addition that hurts it. Build randomization is stripped out, leaving only randomized map portions and enemies. He would recommend it to some people for the visuals, but says it would be much better if it were not a roguelike. He places it in low B.
praise: Visuals and art direction look amazing
Strong world and story as a Metroidvania
Unique genre mix of Metroidvania and roguelike
He enjoyed playing and streaming it for the look
criticism: Roguelike elements feel tacked on and make no sense for the game
No random build aspect, only randomized map pieces and enemies
Randomized platforming within maps is clunky and frustrating
Enemies pop up randomly in levels not designed for them
Randomness hurts what would otherwise be a great game
unique_points: Metroidvania-roguelike hybrid where the world is fixed but rooms' platforming and enemy spawns are randomized
Design lesson: randomization must fit level design, or it undermines it
commentary.quote: this game has no right being a roguelike
design_criteria: Randomization and level design: random platforming and enemy spawns clash with planned levels
Build variety: lacks random build elements, weakening roguelike identity
Visuals and charm: a major strength
Genre fit: roguelike elements feel forced onto a Metroidvania

community.one_liner: A hand-drawn Lovecraftian Metroidvania from Thunder Lotus (Jotun) with procedurally assembled maps, endless enemy horde rooms, and a corruption-based power system.
community.consensus_summary: Sundered is well liked overall: Steam shows Very Positive (about 82%, roughly 5,200 reviews), and Metacritic sits at a Mixed-or-Average 74 from 39 critics, with user score 7.1. Nearly everyone praises the hand-drawn art, animation, atmosphere, boss designs and the fluid movement and abilities. The split is over the core design: the endless horde spawns, semi-procedural maps and stat-driven progression delight some players and feel repetitive and tedious to others. It is a finished 2017 release (Eldritch Edition added the free Magnate of the Gong update with new areas and local co-op); it is not early access. Some recent Steam reviewers mention a dip in recent ratings, and the top positive reviews push back on it.
best_things: Gorgeous hand-drawn art and fluid animation, the most universally praised element (Thunder Lotus signature, compared with Jotun and Spiritfarer)
Large, memorable boss fights that reward learning patterns
Movement and traversal feel great, and new abilities (especially corrupted versions via eldritch shards) make you feel powerful
Atmospheric Lovecraftian world, soundtrack and sparse, evocative lore with a narrator voice and multiple endings
Sprawling central skill tree and build variety give a real sense of progression after each death
Procedural layout keeps exploration fresh and makes a blend of Metroidvania and roguelite that some call the most meaningful one they have played
Non-linear exploration and currency collection, plus difficulty options and easy 100% achievements for completionists
worst_things: Endless horde rooms and waves of weak, repeated enemy types (palette swaps) feel overwhelming, spammy and screen-covering
Combat is described as button mashing or dodging, with little depth outside bosses
Long stretches of empty or samey rooms; the map is not very helpful and the start is confusing with little explanation
Some boss fights are considered poorly designed (either trivial with the right build or slow and tanky)
Local co-op is widely called a letdown: the second player cannot die, collect items or meaningfully interact
Keyboard play suffers, notably the grappling hook section (works far better on a gamepad)
Story is told obliquely and is easy to miss or forget; it is also short (roughly 10 to 20 hours)
improvements: Clearer onboarding and tutorials, including explaining shard destruction and corruption mechanics
More enemy variety and less reliance on palette-swapped stronger variants
Better map and navigation clarity in a procedurally assembled world
A meaningful co-op design where player two has health and can interact with the world
More flexible save slots, since players say the three slots limit getting all endings without replaying
Clearer storytelling and more content or length
unique_things: Resist or Embrace system: corrupt abilities with eldritch shards for power at the cost of humanity, leading to different endings
Procedurally assembled Metroidvania map with handcrafted elements rather than a fixed hand-built world
Horde-based combat where huge numbers of enemies spawn continuously in some rooms
Roguelite-style permanent upgrades via a central skill tree that let you come back stronger after death
Lovecraftian setting in an abandoned underground military base with huge boss sprites
tedious_or_disliked: Endless enemy respawns that force you to stop and fight while chipping away at your health, then chase you back through rooms
Grinding perks and shards; guides reportedly recommend AFK or boss farming for money, which players read as a flawed progression loop
Three endings requiring separate playthroughs, repeating the same path and looting
Running through many empty rooms to get from A to B
Overly complex skill tree with few exciting unlocks for some players
Early game frustration before upgrades arrive
divisive_points: Procedural generation: some love the replayability, others say it undercuts what makes a Metroidvania (authored level design)
Horde mechanic: seen as fitting chaotic eldritch atmosphere by fans and as an annoying pacing killer by detractors
Difficulty and feel of combat: empowering and smooth once upgraded vs. shallow and sloppy
Value and length: worth it at the price for many, bare-bones and only decent on sale for others
community.reception_notes: Launched July 2017 to generally strong reviews from outlets such as GameSpot (8), Eurogamer and Rock, Paper, Shotgun per the Steam page, while the Metacritic aggregate is a more modest 74 because of mid-range scores tied to repetition. The Eldritch Edition added the free Magnate of the Gong update (new areas, quest chains, a boss, local co-op). Platforms: Windows, Mac and Linux on Steam; Steam Deck and controller support noted in reviews (keyboard play is weaker). Estimated 200k to 500k Steam owners and about $2.9M gross revenue (third-party Boxleiter-style estimate, not audited). Several long-time players say recent Steam ratings have dipped to Mixed and call it undeserved; negatives cite the horde design and co-op.
